sentences.text: Two raccoons reached a creek that was higher than it had been in the morning.
Flat stones made a broken line from one bank to the other.
The first raccoon hurried, chose a shiny stone, and slipped.
The slip was not a bad fall. It was a cold splash and a surprised squeak.
The raccoon climbed back onto the bank, shook, and sat down to look again.
This time the pair tested each stone with one paw before trusting it.
If a stone wobbled, they skipped it and chose the next one.
They also waited while a push of water went by, instead of fighting the current.
Halfway across, a branch rushed past and bumped the line of stones, but the stones held.
The raccoons kept the same careful pattern and stepped onto the far mud.
The first try had been fast. The second try was slower and finished the crossing.
Speed had looked bold, but testing the stones had actually worked.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A careful second try that gets the raccoons across
A branch that builds a wooden bridge
A creek that dries up before noon
A shiny stone that can never get wet

questions.explanation: The fast first try ends in a splash. Testing each stone gets them to the far bank. Careful trying is the main idea.

choices.text: They test every stone with a paw
One raccoon hurries, picks a shiny stone, and slips
A branch bumps the line of stones
They step onto the far mud

questions.explanation: The hurried slip is the first try. Testing stones, the passing branch, and the far bank all happen after they start again.

questions.prompt: What do the raccoons do if a stone wobbles?

choices.text: They sit on it until it stops
They throw it into the trees
They skip it and choose the next stone
They call for a larger animal

questions.explanation: The story says that if a stone wobbled, they skipped it and chose the next one. That is a specific step in the second try.

questions.prompt: What can a reader figure out about the shiny stone?

choices.text: Shiny stones are always the safest choice
The stone slipped because it was afraid
The creek only wets dull stones
Looking shiny did not mean it was steady

questions.explanation: The raccoon chooses the stone because it looks shiny, then slips. The story never says shiny means safe. The splash is the clue.
